relations.rationale: Both claims concern shift assignments but involve different people pairs, so one doesn't directly establish the other.
Shift differences between Nell and Leo have no bearing on age differences between Jun and Hugo.
Nell and Leo working different shifts is consistent with there being two shifts, supporting the idea of multiple shifts existing.
If the windows fog up, this directly causes the blurred view of the courtyard described in B.
Oven heat causing fogged windows is unrelated to the smell of cinnamon rolls drifting through the door.
Fogged windows blurring the courtyard view has no connection to Hugo and Leo's shift schedules.
Ranking highest in seniority directly supports having worked there the longest among those present.
Hugo and Leo working different shifts supports the existence of multiple (two) shifts at the shop.
Jun being younger than Hugo has no bearing on whether they handle delivery routes with equal care.
The smell drifting through the door directly supports it drawing in customers from the lane.
The smell of cinnamon rolls has no logical connection to how many shifts the shop runs.
The smell drifting through the door is unrelated to the team gathering outside at day's end.
Customers being drawn in by smell has no bearing on the number of shifts run.
Empty trays by afternoon suggest the day's baking work was done, consistent with the team later gathering to enjoy sunlight before locking up, though not a strict logical requirement.
